title: GPU lane quarantine and transactional quota settlements
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight GPU lane quarantine mechanism combined with a transactional quota settlement system so that bursty or misbehaving tenants can be quickly isolated without disrupting committed throughput guarantees for other tenants.

Background: Dedicated pools currently rely on soft token-bucket throttles and coarse eviction. We still see episodes where a noisy tenant's ephemeral kernels degrade tail latency for colocated tenants during short traffic spikes. Existing approaches (hard slicing, permanent eviction) either reduce utilization or require expensive manual interventions.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a quarantine lane: a temporary isolated scheduling lane on the GPU host that requests can be moved into when they trigger noisy-neighbor detectors. Quarantine lanes have stricter concurrency limits, preemptible helper kernels, and a short time-to-live (configurable).
- Transactional quota settlements: when a tenant consumes burst credits from a global reservoir or cross-tenant burst pool, record the consumption as a transaction and reconcile during the tenant's next billing/window interval. Settlement policies allow reconciliation via cost offsets, throttled refunds, or automatic throttles when quota is exhausted.
- Detection signals: high tail latency (p95->p99 regressions), increased kernel preemption counts, sustained GPU memory pressure, and KV-cache miss spikes. Multiple signals combined using a lightweight scoring function to avoid false positives.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler can classify a spike as legitimate demand (scale out) or noisy (quarantine) based on recent allocation patterns, historic burst behavior, and model size. Quarantine should be preferred when scale failure or long provisioning delay would break other tenants' SLOs.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Prefer transient quarantine to hard-slicing to preserve utilization for normal periods.
- Transactional settlements introduce reconciliation complexity but decouple enforcement from immediate request rejection, improving customer UX for short bursts.
- Detection thresholds tuned conservatively to avoid chasing noisy microbursts.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Quarantine lanes can be activated automatically within 5s of trigger detection and enforce resource caps such that affected tenant's requests do not cause >5% p99 regression on adjacent tenants in repro tests.
- Transactions for burst consumption are logged and visible in Console; settlement completes within the configured billing window and matches audit logs.
- Autoscaler respects quarantine signals and does not perform scale-downs that would move quarantined workloads back into shared lanes prematurely.

Deliverables:
- Host-level quarantine controller, scheduling hooks in lane allocator, and runtime guardrails to mark requests as quarantined.
- Transaction ledger service (append-only) for burst usage events and reconciliation worker (batched).
- Console dashboard showing quarantine incidents, per-tenant burst ledger, and reconciliation status.
- E2E test harness and canary rollout plan for dedicated clusters.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and proposal drafted. Pulled metrics from incident 2026-02-02 where a single tenant spike increased p99 by 18% across 4 hosts. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DED/GPU+Quarantine+Design

2026-02-18 - Marcus Li: Ran a small local sim that injects KV-cache misses; quarantine activation latency ~4.2s. Need to reduce detection false positives; suggest combining preemption_count + tail_latency with a sliding window. See prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/r-runtime/pull/5123

2026-02-24 - Sofia Martinez (SRE): Raised concern about transactional ledger durability and cross-region reconciliation. Recommend using existing raft-backed store or leveraging events via Kafka with idempotent consumers. Logged ADR: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ARCH/ADR+-+Burst+Ledger

2026-03-02 - Product review (Jonah Reed): Prioritize visibility in Console before enforcement. Add a "dry-run" quarantine mode that marks incidents but does not move traffic for the first 2 weeks of canary.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Li: Implemented dry-run mode; console annotation added. Integration tests for quarantine cap enforcement to follow. WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/compare/quarantine-proto

2026-03-09 - Security (Lina Cho): Confirmed transactional ledger should be encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Suggested KMS usage and audit logging. Raised minimal impact to threat model. Security ticket: ENG-833210

2026-03-10 - Marcus Li: Merged scheduler hooks for lane tagging behind feature flag. Next: implement reconciliation worker and console panels. Blocked: need QA test data for settlement scenarios (refunds, throttles).
acceptance_criteria: Automatic quarantine activation within 5s for composite detection triggers in repro harness
Quarantine lane enforces configured caps; repro tests show <=5% p99 regression for adjacent tenants
Transactional burst events emitted to ledger with idempotent keys and visible in Console within 60s
Settlement worker completes reconciliation within billing window and writes audit entries
Dry-run mode exists and is used during canary; enforcement only enabled after 2-week observation period
Feature gated behind runtime.featureFlags.quarantine and rollout plan documented
